nodes.label: Worker Bundle Size Check (3072 KiB budget)
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare's 3MiB free-plan script-size rejection was only discovered at the real wrangler deploy step, after build already ran (e.g. @react-pdf/renderer's PDFKit dependency silently pushed the script over the limit, three separate times). A dry-run deploy reports the same gzipped size without touching the live Worker, so this fails fast with a clear message. Budget is set to the real 3072 KiB hard limit (not a conservative number) because the app is already at ~3052 KiB gzipped with only ~20 KiB headroom; a tighter budget would fail CI on every deploy even though nothing is broken. Real headroom must come from removing bundle weight (the @react-pdf/renderer -> jsPDF swap bought back ~900 KiB once already).
nodes.norm_label: worker bundle size check (3072 kib budget)

nodes.label: DATABASE_URL Secret Format Correction Step
nodes.rationale: `wrangler secret put <key>` has no `--value` flag (confirmed via a real CI failure: 'Unknown argument: value'); the documented mechanism is reading the value from stdin via a shell pipe, which cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3's `command:` input can't express, so wrangler is called directly here instead. This step exists specifically because DATABASE_URL is the one secret with a previously-undocumented, non-obvious correct format (direct endpoint, no -pooler, no channel_binding); all other live secrets are left untouched by this workflow.

nodes.label: Verify Live Health After Deploy Step
nodes.rationale: Every prior deploy through this pipeline was manually checked with a one-off curl against /api/health afterward; this step makes that check part of the pipeline instead of relying on a human to remember, with retries since a fresh Worker version can take a moment to propagate.
nodes.norm_label: verify live health after deploy step

nodes.label: Two Backends Coexistence Decision
nodes.rationale: Explicit decision to keep both the live Next.js/Supabase app and the NestJS+TypeORM `/backend` migration target side by side for now — this is not a cutover in progress, it's two things that exist together until the team decides otherwise. Don't assume code in one implies the other is current; they're maintained by different passes.

nodes.label: Missing CRON_SECRET Risk
nodes.rationale: Without CRON_SECRET set, scheduled cron jobs (/api/cron/*) 401 silently, every day, forever — called out as the highest-impact missing config for a real deploy.

nodes.label: Switching Resume Storage to SharePoint
nodes.rationale: Code (src/lib/integrations/sharepoint.ts, src/lib/resumeStorage.ts) was built and tested as far as possible without a real Microsoft 365 tenant: default Supabase path confirmed unchanged, SharePoint mode confirmed to fail with a clear specific error rather than crash or silently no-op. Real upload/download against an actual tenant was never tested — flagged as the one piece of the handover needing a human with real M365 access.

nodes.label: AI Provider Nuance — NVIDIA Kimi Tool-Call Degeneration
nodes.rationale: Only NVIDIA has ever been live-tested (no Anthropic key was ever available). Confirmed across 6+ live request variations: NVIDIA's moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 reliably calls a tool but degenerates into repeated tokens a meaningful fraction of the time right after consuming the tool's result. Reliable for single-shot generation only, which is why the daily digest uses single-shot, not tool-calling. Mitigations (penalty params + looksDegenerate() fallback) reduce but don't eliminate the failure rate — prefer Anthropic once a key exists.
nodes.norm_label: ai provider nuance — nvidia kimi tool-call degeneration

nodes.label: Backend (NestJS) Status
nodes.rationale: Every entity carries is_deleted/deleted_at via BaseEntity but no live Supabase table has those columns today, so pointing this backend at production data will fail until a migration adds them. Auth provider is switching from Supabase Auth to Clerk, requiring a one-time user-mapping script before any existing account can log in. Most of the app isn't ported yet.

nodes.label: Cost-Efficient Deployment Recommendations
nodes.rationale: Recommends Vercel (Hobby free / Pro $20/seat for commercial-use compliance), keeping the existing Supabase project rather than provisioning a second Postgres for the NestJS backend, Fly.io/Railway for NestJS compute, Clerk once migrated, and SharePoint for resume storage — realistic total $2-7/month on free tiers, $25-32/month if Vercel Pro/Supabase paid tier are needed.

nodes.rationale: Strategy: Hybrid Option A — Neon becomes the main app database while Supabase Auth and Storage remain temporarily; full auth/storage independence deferred to a future Phase 2 sprint.

nodes.label: Mandatory Verification Checklist (typecheck/lint/build/bundle-size/live-schema)
nodes.rationale: Required because a prior contributor pushed a build without confirming typecheck/lint/build actually passed (npm/npx not in PATH), and because assuming a column/table name instead of checking the live schema directly caused multiple real bugs earlier in the session (e.g. application_resume_versions has no application_id column, application_packets was missing 10 assumed columns).

nodes.label: Broken Upload Flow Problem (pdf-parse Node-only)
nodes.rationale: pdf-parse is Node.js-only and breaks on Cloudflare Workers; the current extractText() using Buffer.from() and pdf-parse is unreliable, and SharePoint upload errors are swallowed instead of shown to the user.

nodes.label: Separate Python Markitdown Microservice Decision
nodes.rationale: Markitdown requires Python and has no JS equivalent of the same quality; TalentOS is TypeScript/Next.js deployed to Cloudflare Workers (edge runtime, no Python), so a separate stateless HTTP microservice is standard microservices architecture rather than trying to run Python on the edge.

nodes.label: Token Savings from Markdown vs Raw Text Parsing
nodes.rationale: Raw extracted text is noisy and loses formatting, costing ~3000-5000 tokens per resume parse; markdown is cleaner for AI parsing, reducing cost to ~1500-2500 tokens — an estimated 40-50% token savings per resume parse.
nodes.norm_label: token savings from markdown vs raw text parsing

nodes.label: Second Provider: NVIDIA-hosted moonshotai/kimi-k2.6
nodes.rationale: Live-tested finding: the model reliably decides to call a tool but degenerates into repeated tokens (finish_reason: 'repetition') consuming the tool's result a meaningful fraction of the time — reproduced across 6+ request variations, indicating the model/endpoint itself under this pattern, not a request-format bug. Mitigated with frequency/presence penalty and a looksDegenerate() fallback; Anthropic preferred once available.

nodes.rationale: Status: infrastructure prepared, preview not yet run, deploy not yet attempted. Auth/Storage strategy is Hybrid Option A (keep Supabase Auth/Storage temporarily, Neon for app database) — the safest path given how deeply Supabase Auth is embedded (4 files) and that ~120 files still use supabase.from().

nodes.label: Auth Migration: Supabase Auth → Clerk
nodes.rationale: profiles.user_id (Supabase auth.users.id) becomes profiles.id (internal UUID) plus a separate clerk_user_id column; the data migration script must map old Supabase auth user IDs to Clerk user IDs before importing profile-owned records.

nodes.label: RLS → Application-Level Authorization Migration
nodes.rationale: Supabase RLS was enabled with no policies because the Next app used the service-role key server-side; in NestJS, authorization moves to AuthorizationService.profileFor()/requireRole()/assertApplicationVisibility(), which ports the exact application-engineer visibility rule from the live app.

nodes.label: Ad-Hoc Application Creation (No Job Masterlist Required)
nodes.rationale: Applications must currently reference a job from the master list, costing an AE ~2-3 minutes of data entry per application (2+ hours/day at 50 applications/day); making job_id nullable and storing adhoc_job_data JSONB removes that gate.
nodes.norm_label: ad-hoc application creation (no job masterlist required)

nodes.label: Auto-Create Job from Pasted JD
nodes.rationale: Pasted JDs previously went only into target_jobs.raw_description with zero knowledge reuse; AI extraction plus fuzzy-match deduplication (Levenshtein on company+title+location, >85% similarity) lets every pasted JD enrich the shared jobs masterlist.

nodes.label: Bypass Base Resume Option (Original Resume / Blank)
nodes.rationale: Requiring a base resume before an application can be created creates a hard dependency and pressure to build resumes before knowing if a candidate is a fit; adding source_type (base_resume/original_resume/blank/manual) removes that gate.

nodes.label: Web Crypto API Rewrites (Security-Critical)
nodes.rationale: secretCrypto.ts, webhookEngine.ts, and publicApiAuth.ts are rewritten to use crypto.subtle instead of Node's crypto module so encryption/HMAC/hashing work on both Node.js and Cloudflare Workers.

nodes.label: POST /generate Endpoint (Vertex AI Gemini Bridge)
nodes.rationale: Minimal Cloud Run proxy bridges the TalentOS Cloudflare Worker to Vertex AI Gemini using Cloud Run service identity / Application Default Credentials, so no API key or service account JSON needs to be embedded in the Worker.

nodes.label: 10-Minute Cron Trigger (Render Keepalive)
nodes.rationale: Pings the Render-hosted markitdown service's /health endpoint every 10 minutes to keep it warm between real requests, staying below Render's usual 15-minute inactivity window; removable once/if Render is upgraded to an always-on paid plan.

nodes.label: app_number Migration-Never-Ran Production Bug
nodes.rationale: sql/05_neon_fixes.sql (now 001_app_number_and_timestamps.sql) was written but never actually run against Neon; code depending on its applications.app_number column shipped and broke production before anyone noticed — the fix existed, it just never executed. This directory exists so every .sql file here is auto-run by deploy.yml on every deploy, in filename order.

nodes.label: Additive-Only Idempotency Rules for neon_fixes
nodes.rationale: Every statement must be safe to run unlimited times against a database already in any state (CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, guarded DO $$ blocks); no DROP TABLE or data-deleting statements, since CI runs this unattended on every push with no review gate before it executes against production.
